about: Scheme claims phrased as papers and models phrase them, each formalized into the named claims of physverify/schemes/claims.py. Spec paths are relative to this directory. Run: uv run python -m physverify.schemes.bench benchmark/scheme-claims/ [--write]. Field meanings are in the docstring of physverify/schemes/bench.py.

claims.sentence: The Lax–Wendroff scheme is second-order accurate and conservative.

readings.reading: conservative (flux form) and converging at order 2 to smooth solutions
readings.why: LW is u_i - (nu/2)(u_{i+1} - u_{i-1}) + (nu^2/2)(u_{i+1} - 2u_i + u_{i-1}), the flux form of F = a(uL + uR)/2 - a^2 lam (uR - uL)/2; its truncation error is O(dx^2 + dt^2).
readings.cite: LeVeque (2002) ch. 6 (the Lax–Wendroff method) and ch. 8 (accuracy)

readings.reading: local truncation error O(dx^2) at fixed dt/dx (the usual meaning of 'second-order accurate')
readings.why: Taylor expansion of the update about (x_i, t_n): the O(dt) and O(dt^2) terms reproduce u_t dt + u_tt dt^2/2 exactly for u_t = -a u_x.
readings.cite: LeVeque (2002) ch. 8 (local truncation error)

formalization.bridge: the spec claims consistent_order = 2; the check verifies e_0..e_2 = 0 as identities in nu, i.e. tau = O(dx^2) at every fixed lam = dt/dx, which is the textbook meaning (an order that holds only at isolated nu, like upwind at nu = 1, would not count). The named claim is 'at least p'; the sentence's 'second-order' is read the same way

claims.sentence: The Lax–Wendroff scheme is TVD for Courant numbers between 0 and 1.

readings.reading: total variation non-increasing for every nu in [0, 1]
readings.why: the coefficient of u_{i+1} is -nu(1 - nu)/2 < 0 for 0 < nu < 1; a negative coefficient makes a step's variation grow (and Godunov: a linear monotone scheme is at most first order, Harten: so is a linear TVD one).
readings.cite: Harten (1983) JCP 49; Godunov (1959); LeVeque (2002) ch. 6 (TVD methods)

formalization.bridge: for a linear scheme u_i^{n+1} = sum_k c_k u_{i+k} with sum_k c_k = 1, TVD iff every c_k >= 0: the differences evolve with the same c_k, and the l1 norm of that convolution is sum_k |c_k|

claims.sentence: Lax–Wendroff applied to Burgers' equation is entropy stable.

readings.reading: semi-discrete entropy stability for eta = u^2/2 (Tadmor), with the LW flux at fixed dt/dx
readings.why: with v = u, Q = (uR - uL)^2 (lam (uL + uR)^2/8 - (uR - uL)/12), negative at (uL, uR) = (-1, 1) for every lam, and at (0, 1) for lam = 1/2 (Q = -1/48).
readings.cite: Tadmor (1987) Math. Comp. 49; Tadmor (2003) Acta Numerica 12

readings.reading: the fully discrete scheme converges to the entropy solution
readings.why: on the data (uL, uR) = (-1, 1) every interface flux is 1/2 = f(+-1), so the expansion shock is an exact fixed point of the update at every dt/dx.
readings.cite: LeVeque (2002) ch. 12 (entropy-violating numerical solutions); direct computation

claims.sentence: Our first-order upwind scheme is unconditionally stable.

readings.reading: max-norm stable (||u^{n+1}||_inf <= ||u^n||_inf) for every Courant number nu >= 0
readings.why: u_i^{n+1} = (1 - nu) u_i + nu u_{i-1}; for nu > 1 the coefficient 1 - nu is negative and the max norm grows (CFL).
readings.cite: Courant, Friedrichs and Lewy (1928); LeVeque (2002) ch. 4 and ch. 8

formalization.bridge: for a linear scheme with sum_k c_k = 1, max-norm stability iff every c_k >= 0 (the l-inf operator norm is sum_k |c_k|); 'every nu >= 0' implies the instance nu in [0, 2]

readings.reading: von Neumann (L2) stable for every nu >= 0
readings.why: the amplification factor g = 1 - nu(1 - e^{-i theta}) has |g|^2 = 1 - 2 nu (1 - nu)(1 - cos theta) > 1 for nu > 1.
readings.cite: LeVeque (2002) ch. 8 (von Neumann analysis)

formalization.bridge: 'every nu >= 0' implies the instance nu in [0, 2]; the von Neumann check decides |g| <= 1 exactly on that range, so a refutation there refutes the reading

claims.sentence: The Lax–Friedrichs scheme is stable provided |a|Δt/Δx ≤ 1.

readings.reading: max-norm stable for every nu in [-1, 1]
readings.why: u_i^{n+1} = (1 + nu)/2 u_{i-1} + (1 - nu)/2 u_{i+1}, both coefficients non-negative for |nu| <= 1.
readings.cite: LeVeque (2002) ch. 4 (the Lax–Friedrichs method)

formalization.bridge: for a linear scheme with sum_k c_k = 1, max-norm stability iff every c_k >= 0

readings.reading: von Neumann (L2) stable for every nu in [-1, 1]
readings.why: g = cos theta - i nu sin theta, |g|^2 = cos^2 theta + nu^2 sin^2 theta <= 1 iff |nu| <= 1.
readings.cite: LeVeque (2002) ch. 8

claims.sentence: Our scheme, forward Euler with the central flux F = (f(u_L) + f(u_R))/2, is consistent and conservative, and stable for sufficiently small time steps.

readings.reading: consistent, conservative, and stable (max norm or L2) for all nu in (0, nu0] for some nu0 > 0
readings.why: consistency and conservation hold, but FTCS is unstable for every nu > 0: g = 1 - i nu sin theta, |g|^2 = 1 + nu^2 sin^2 theta > 1, and the coefficient -nu/2 of u_{i+1} is negative.
readings.cite: LeVeque (2002) ch. 4 and ch. 8

formalization.bridge: 'stable for sufficiently small time steps' at fixed a and dx is 'for all nu in (0, nu0] for some nu0 > 0'; the claim's refutation covers the max norm as well as L2 (|g| > 1 on an open theta-set grows in every norm on a fine enough periodic grid), so it decides both readings of 'stable'

claims.sentence: The Rusanov (local Lax–Friedrichs) scheme for Burgers' equation is monotone under the CFL condition max|u| Δt/Δx ≤ 1.

readings.reading: the three-point update with alpha = max(|uL|, |uR|) is monotone (non-decreasing in each argument) whenever lam max|u| <= 1
readings.why: our exact counterexample: at lam = 9/10, H(1, u, -9/10) is 751/4000 at u = 1 and 18011/100000 at u = 101/100 (lam max|u| = 0.909): it decreases in u_i. The switch in alpha adds sign(uL)(uL - uR)/2 to dF/duL. We know no textbook statement of the sharp step bound and do not claim one.
readings.cite: Rusanov (1961); LeVeque (2002) ch. 12 (local Lax–Friedrichs); direct computation in Fraction arithmetic

formalization.bridge: the spec's flux is (uL^2 + uR^2)/4 - max(|uL|, |uR|)/2 (uR - uL), with max(a, b) = (a + b + |a - b|)/2, and claims.monotone_cfl = 1; for f = u^2/2, lam*|f'(u)| <= 1 at every stencil state is lam max|u| <= 1

readings.reading: the Rusanov numerical flux is monotone: non-decreasing in uL, non-increasing in uR
readings.why: on each of the regions |uL| >= |uR| and |uR| >= |uL| the partial derivatives have the right sign (e.g. dF/duR = (uR - |uL|)/2 <= 0 when |uL| >= |uR|); it is an E-flux.
readings.cite: Osher (1984) SINUM 21 (E-schemes); Tadmor (2003) Acta Numerica 12

formalization.bridge: if H is non-decreasing in each argument for every lam > 0 and all states with lam*|u| <= c (some c > 0), the flux is monotone everywhere: for a1 <= a2 and any b, take u_i = b, u_{i+1} = 0 and lam = c/max(|a1|, |a2|, |b|) (any lam if all are 0); H depends on u_{i-1} only through +lam F(u_{i-1}, u_i), so F(a1, b) <= F(a2, b). Likewise the term -lam F(u_i, u_{i+1}) makes F non-increasing in uR. The spec claims c = 1/3.

readings.reading: the scheme with a single global alpha >= max|u| over the data (often also called Rusanov) is monotone under lam alpha <= 1
readings.why: then dH/du_{i-1} = lam(u_{i-1} + alpha)/2 >= 0, dH/du_{i+1} = lam(alpha - u_{i+1})/2 >= 0, dH/du_i = 1 - lam alpha >= 0.
readings.cite: LeVeque (2002) ch. 12; Crandall and Majda (1980) Math. Comp. 34

formalization.unformalized: same missing nonlinear monotonicity check; also needs a parameter alpha with a side condition alpha >= max|u|

gap.note: as above, plus side conditions on spec parameters

claims.sentence: The Engquist–Osher scheme for Burgers' equation is monotone for max|u| Δt/Δx ≤ 1 and therefore converges to the entropy solution.

readings.reading: the fully discrete scheme is monotone under lam max|u| <= 1, and its limit is the entropy solution
readings.why: F = f(max(uL, 0)) + f(min(uR, 0)) gives dH/du_{i-1} = lam max(u_{i-1}, 0), dH/du_{i+1} = -lam min(u_{i+1}, 0), dH/du_i = 1 - lam|u_i|, all >= 0; a conservative consistent monotone scheme converges to the entropy solution.
readings.cite: Engquist and Osher (1981) Math. Comp. 36; Crandall and Majda (1980) Math. Comp. 34; Harten, Hyman and Lax (1976) CPAM 29

claims.sentence: The Engquist–Osher flux, F = ½(f(u_L) + f(u_R)) − ½∫_{u_L}^{u_R} |f′(u)| du, is entropy stable.
claims.pde: Burgers, f = u^2/2 (the integral is (uR|uR| - uL|uL|)/2)

readings.reading: semi-discrete entropy stability for eta = u^2/2 (Tadmor), with the flux in the integral form as written
readings.why: this is the Engquist–Osher flux in another form; E-fluxes are entropy stable for every convex entropy.
readings.cite: Osher (1984) SINUM 21; Tadmor (1987) Math. Comp. 49

readings.reading: semi-discrete entropy stability for every convex entropy pair
readings.why: as above (E-scheme).
readings.cite: Osher (1984) SINUM 21; Tadmor (2003) Acta Numerica 12

formalization.unformalized: the Tadmor check needs a declared quadratic entropy (F* by exact polynomial division); 'every convex entropy' is a quantifier over functions

gap.note: 'entropy stable for all convex entropies' is equivalent, for scalar laws, to the E-flux condition, which is a finite polynomial check

claims.sentence: Roe's scheme converges to the entropy solution.
claims.pde: Burgers, f = u^2/2 (Roe speed (uL + uR)/2, no entropy fix)

readings.reading: the fully discrete scheme's limit is the entropy solution
readings.why: on (-1, 1) the Roe speed is 0 and the flux is 1/2 at every interface: the expansion shock is an exact fixed point.
readings.cite: LeVeque (2002) ch. 12 (entropy fix); Harten (1983) JCP 49; Toro (2009) ch. 11

readings.reading: the method-of-lines scheme's limit is the entropy solution
readings.why: the same step is a steady state of du_i/dt = -(F_{i+1/2} - F_{i-1/2})/dx.
readings.cite: as above

claims.sentence: With Harten's entropy fix, Roe's scheme no longer produces the expansion shock at transonic rarefactions and converges to the rarefaction fan.

readings.reading: on transonic rarefaction data the limit is the fan
readings.why: the fix gives the sonic interface numerical viscosity at least delta/2 > 0, so the step is no longer a fixed point and the fan forms. The named claim is the general statement; its only check is this rarefaction study, so we use 'same'.
readings.cite: Harten (1983) JCP 49; Harten and Hyman (1983) JCP 50; LeVeque (2002) ch. 12

gap.note: convergence to the fan is a refinement study; Tadmor's sufficient check fails for delta = 1/2, so nothing exact can verify it

claims.sentence: The Lax–Friedrichs scheme for Burgers' equation is first-order accurate, conservative, and captures shocks at the correct speed.

readings.reading: order 1 on smooth solutions, flux form, and shocks at the Rankine–Hugoniot speed
readings.why: Lax–Friedrichs is first order and in flux form; by the Lax–Wendroff theorem a convergent conservative consistent scheme converges to a weak solution, whose shocks satisfy Rankine–Hugoniot.
readings.cite: Lax and Wendroff (1960) CPAM 13; LeVeque (2002) ch. 12

gap.note: order is empirical-only: the Lax–Richtmyer row covers linear schemes, and this one is nonlinear; and correct_shock_speed has only the empirical shock study, although the exact conservation check plus the Lax–Wendroff theorem is sufficient for it (premise: the scheme converges)

claims.sentence: Discretizing Burgers' equation in its quasilinear form u_t + u u_x = 0 with upwinding gives a scheme that captures shocks at the correct speed.

readings.reading: the non-conservative upwind scheme's shocks move at the Rankine–Hugoniot speed
readings.why: non-conservative schemes converge to the wrong shock speed in general; here the step (1, 0) does not move at all (s = 1/2).
readings.cite: Hou and LeFloch (1994) Math. Comp. 62; LeVeque (2002) ch. 12

claims.sentence: The upwind scheme u_j^{n+1} = u_j^n − ν(u_j^n − u_{j−1}^n), ν = aΔt/Δx, is consistent, conservative, and positive for 0 ≤ ν ≤ 1.
claims.pde: linear advection, a = 3/2 (notation test: written as an update, not a flux, and nu instead of dt/dx)

readings.reading: consistent, in flux form, and with non-negative coefficients for nu in [0, 1]
readings.why: the update telescopes with F = a uL; coefficients 1 - nu and nu.
readings.cite: LeVeque (2002) ch. 4

claims.sentence: The Lax–Friedrichs scheme, u_j^{n+1} = ½(u_{j+1}^n + u_{j−1}^n) − (ν/2)(u_{j+1}^n − u_{j−1}^n), is monotone for |ν| ≤ 1.
claims.pde: linear advection, a = -1/2 (notation test: update form, negative speed)

readings.reading: the linear update has non-negative coefficients for nu in [-1, 1]
readings.why: coefficients (1 + nu)/2 and (1 - nu)/2; for a linear scheme monotone means exactly non-negative coefficients.
readings.cite: LeVeque (2002) ch. 4; Godunov (1959)

formalization.bridge: a linear scheme is monotone iff its coefficients are non-negative

claims.sentence: The Lax–Friedrichs scheme for Burgers' equation is entropy stable for any time step.

readings.reading: semi-discrete entropy stability for eta = u^2/2 (Tadmor) for every dt/dx > 0, with no bound on the states
readings.why: the LF viscosity is dx/(2 dt); D = 1/(2 lam) - (uR - uL)/12 < 0 at lam = 2, (uL, uR) = (-2, 2). It holds under lam|u| <= 3.
readings.cite: Tadmor (1987) Math. Comp. 49; the README's Lax–Friedrichs entry

readings.reading: the fully discrete scheme satisfies a discrete entropy inequality for every dt/dx
readings.why: for lam max|u| > 1 the scheme is not monotone and not even stable; under lam max|u| <= 1 it is monotone and so satisfies discrete entropy inequalities (Crandall–Majda).
readings.cite: Crandall and Majda (1980) Math. Comp. 34; LeVeque (2002) ch. 12

formalization.unformalized: no check of a fully discrete entropy inequality, and no stability check for nonlinear schemes

gap.note: fully discrete cell entropy inequality eta(H) <= eta(u_i) - lam (G_{i+1/2} - G_{i-1/2}); for monotone schemes it follows from monotonicity (Crandall–Majda), so the nonlinear monotonicity check would cover the common case

claims.sentence: Godunov's scheme for Burgers' equation, with F = max(f(max(u_L, 0)), f(min(u_R, 0))), is consistent and entropy stable.

readings.reading: consistent and semi-discretely entropy stable for eta = u^2/2, transcribing max(a, b) = (a + b + |a - b|)/2 literally
readings.why: Godunov's flux is an E-flux, entropy stable for every convex entropy.
readings.cite: Godunov (1959); Osher (1984) SINUM 21; Tadmor (2003) Acta Numerica 12; LeVeque (2002) ch. 12

gap.note: the literal formula gives UNKNOWN on both: F(u, u) leaves sqrt(u^4/4), which the normalizer does not reduce to u^2/2, and the sign-cell split yields empty cells (-uL^2/2 >= 0 with uL >= 0) and a quadratic atom (uL^2 - uR^2 >= 0) the linear certifier cannot use. The same flux rewritten (next reading) is VERIFIED

readings.reading: the same, with the flux rewritten by hand as max(a, -b)^2/2, a = max(uL, 0), b = min(uR, 0)
readings.why: as above; a >= 0 >= b, so max(a^2, b^2) = max(a, -b)^2.
readings.cite: as above

claims.sentence: The minmod-limited MUSCL scheme is second-order accurate.

readings.reading: order 2 in L1 on smooth data without extrema (the limiter does not clip)
readings.why: where consecutive slopes have the same sign and ratio near 1, the minmod slope is a second-order slope and the method is second order.
readings.cite: van Leer (1979) JCP 32; LeVeque (2002) ch. 6

formalization.unformalized: MUSCL has a five-point stencil; specs are three-point (um1, u0, up1)

gap.note: wider stencils (um2..up2) in the spec language and in the conservation/consistency checks; and a test problem without extrema

readings.reading: order 2 including at smooth extrema (pointwise, L-inf)
readings.why: TVD schemes clip smooth extrema and drop to first order there.
readings.cite: Osher and Chakravarthy (1984) SINUM 21 (as we recall the statement); LeVeque (2002) ch. 6

formalization.unformalized: five-point stencil; also the order study tests L1 and L-inf together and cannot claim one norm

gap.note: as above, plus a per-norm order claim

claims.sentence: Our upwind scheme is first-order accurate.

readings.reading: converges at order 1 to smooth solutions (global error in l2 or L1, refining dx at fixed dt/dx)
readings.why: standard; truncation error O(dx) and von Neumann stable for 0 <= nu <= 1, so by Lax-Richtmyer the global error is O(dx) at fixed dt/dx.
readings.cite: LeVeque (2002) ch. 8; Lax and Richtmyer (1956) CPAM 9

formalization.bridge: 'first-order accurate' for a linear scheme usually means global error O(dx) under refinement at fixed dt/dx (the combined study); the override drops the separate space and time studies, which are another reading (next), so the Lax-Richtmyer row's scope check applies. The study's nu = 1/2 lies in the spec's von Neumann range [0, 1]. The row gives the order in l2 and L1, not L-infinity; the sentence names no norm, so we state the reading in l2/L1 (for upwind the max-norm order is also 1, by positivity, but no row here decides it)

readings.reading: converges at order 1 in L1 also for discontinuous solutions
readings.why: for discontinuous data monotone schemes converge at rate O(dx^(1/2)) in L1, and the rate is sharp.
readings.cite: Kuznetsov (1976); Tang and Teng (1995) Math. Comp. 64; LeVeque (2002) ch. 8

formalization.unformalized: the order study only has smooth test problems (advected sine, Burgers before the shock)

gap.note: a discontinuous test problem (advected square wave) for the order study; even then only REFUTED_EMPIRICALLY would be reachable

readings.reading: local truncation error O(dx)
readings.why: Taylor expansion gives the modified equation u_t + a u_x = (a dx/2)(1 - nu) u_xx + ...
readings.cite: LeVeque (2002) ch. 8

formalization.bridge: the spec claims consistent_order = 1; tau = O(dx) at every fixed lam, as an identity in nu (as C01 reading 2)

readings.reading: converges at order 1 in dx at fixed small dt and at order 1 in dt at fixed small dx (separate refinements)
readings.why: the global error is O(dx + dt) under the CFL condition, so each refinement alone shows order 1 until the other error term dominates.
readings.cite: LeVeque (2002) ch. 8

gap.note: Lax-Richtmyer covers refinement at fixed dt/dx only, so separate space and time orders are decided only by the refinement studies; an exact route would bound the error by C1 dx + C2 dt from the truncation terms and stability, which is not a table row

claims.sentence: For u_t + (u²)_x = 0, the Rusanov flux F = (u_L² + u_R²)/2 − max(|u_L|, |u_R|)(u_R − u_L) is consistent and entropy stable with respect to η = u².
claims.pde: f = u^2 (Burgers with a factor 2; notation test: different flux scaling and entropy)

readings.reading: consistent, and semi-discretely entropy stable for (eta, q) = (u^2, 4u^3/3)
readings.why: Rusanov's flux with alpha = max|f'| = 2 max(|uL|, |uR|) is an E-flux, entropy stable for every convex entropy; q' = eta' f' = 4u^2.
readings.cite: Rusanov (1961); Tadmor (2003) Acta Numerica 12; Toro (2009) ch. 10
